newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa Cargo sees DM40 mln loss in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo sees DM40 mln loss in 1997.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG (LCAG), the cargo subsidiary of Deutsche Lufthansa AG, said it expects stagnating sales revenue in 1996 and 1997.
LCAG chairman Wilhelm Althen told a news conference the airline was likely to make a loss of about 40 million marks in 1997 and would first return to profit in 1998.
He did not disclose his expectations of this year's loss but made it clear it would be difficult to improve the current situation significantly.
Lufthansa Cargo made a loss of 66 million marks over the first three quarters of this year on a turnover of 2.46 billion marks.
It recorded a load factor of 67.9 percent compared to 68.2 percent over the same period last year.
Freight and post carried totalled 1.22 million tonnes compared to 1.15 million tonnes over the nine months of 1995.
In the full 1995 fiscal year, the cargo airline made a profit of 20 million marks on a turnover of 3.5 billion marks.

"This year we will have about the same (turnover) level as last year. I am convinced that next year revenue growth will not be much above that, perhaps about three percent," he said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
